index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure illustrates the architecture of the UH-1 model, which is designed to generate humanoid robot actions from natural language text commands. The overall layout is divided into two main sections: the top section shows the high-level interaction between text representation and the UH-1 Transformer, while the bottom section details the internal structure of the UH-1 Humanoid Action Tokenizer.

In the top section, on the left, there is a purple rectangular box labeled 'Text Representation' containing an example image sequence of a young woman performing exercises in a living room, along with the corresponding text description: 'A young woman is doing a workout in a living room, using her legs and arms to perform various exercises.' This text is processed into a sequence of colored square tokens—ranging from light purple to orange—representing the encoded text input. These tokens are fed into a large light blue rectangular block labeled 'UH-1 Transformer'.

Below the text representation, another rectangular box labeled 'Humanoid Robot Actions' displays a sequence of five black silhouette figures of a humanoid robot performing different motions, connected by a dashed gray curve indicating motion continuity. These actions are converted into a sequence of colored square tokens labeled 'Humanoid Action Tokens', which follow a similar color gradient as the text tokens but end with a purple token, suggesting a variable-length output sequence. These action tokens are generated by the UH-1 Transformer based on the text input.

A horizontal dashed line separates the top section from the bottom section, which focuses on the 'UH-1 Humanoid Action Tokenizer'. On the left side of this section, a vertical stack of three humanoid robot silhouettes represents the input action sequence. An arrow points from this stack to a trapezoidal light blue block labeled 'Encoder'. The encoder processes the input actions and outputs a latent representation denoted by the symbol 'Z' inside a peach-colored rounded rectangle. Below 'Z', four colored square tokens (pink, orange, purple, and yellow) represent the discrete action tokens produced by the tokenizer.

An arrow leads from 'Z' to another trapezoidal light blue block labeled 'Decoder', which reconstructs the original action sequence. The output is shown as a vertical stack of three humanoid robot silhouettes on the right, identical in form to the input, indicating successful reconstruction. A bidirectional dashed arrow spans horizontally across the top of the tokenizer section, connecting the input and output action sequences, emphasizing the auto-encoding nature of the tokenizer.

The entire diagram uses consistent visual elements: rectangular blocks for modules, colored squares for tokens, and arrows for data flow. Text labels are clear and positioned near their respective components. The figure effectively conveys the dual process of action tokenization and text-to-action generation within the UH-1 framework.
